issues.issue: "Repurchase agreements shall mature in one year or less" measured by "the end date of the agreement" gives no rule for open or evergreen repurchase agreements, which have no stated end date. The maturity of such an agreement is therefore indeterminate under this sentence.

The downgrade trigger refers to a security ceasing to have the highest rating "from the requisite NRSROs" and to "an Unrated Security," neither of which is defined here, while c030 requires a rating from only "at least one" NRSRO. The condition that starts the reassessment duty cannot be matched to the quality test it is supposed to police.

Investment in registered and unregistered investment companies "to the extent permitted by law," with only illustrative ("e.g.") examples, leaves the permitted class of investment companies unbounded. The parenthetical examples do not limit the general permission that precedes them.

Authority to invest "some, a significant portion, or all" of the Series' assets in shares of another series of the Trust cannot be squared with c032's 5% single-issuer limit or with the diversification, quality and maturity guidelines in c030 through c041, all of which a wholesale investment in a sister series would bypass. Whether the guidelines apply look-through or not is the resulting question.

"A leading money market index such as Fed Funds or LIBOR" is an open-ended catch-all: "such as" leaves what counts as a "leading" index undetermined, while only dual index and inverse floaters are expressly prohibited. The permitted universe of indices is therefore fixed by neither the general term nor the enumerated examples.

The statement that "the value of the Shares will change with the change in value of the CI Term Trust's investments" cannot be squared with c029's stable $10.00 per Share objective and c007's fixed $10.00 price. Whether investors were told the share value floats or is held constant is left for construction.

The risk paragraph describes the portfolio as "debt securities, such as notes and bonds," a narrower universe than c031's authorized list, which includes asset-backed and mortgage-backed securities, Rule 144A paper and units of other business trusts. Whether the disclosed risks extend to those instruments must be resolved against c031.

Credit risk is described as including "the counterparty to a derivative," yet derivatives appear nowhere in the authorized investments listed in c031. Whether derivatives may be held at all is thrown into doubt by the mismatch between the risk disclosure and the investment policy.

The closing sentence contemplates investing in specific securities "for the purpose of matching the duration of a securities loan entered into for a Shareholder," a Shareholder-specific matching that cannot be squared with c006's undivided pro-rata interest in a commingled Series or with the pooled cash collateral contemplated by the Securities Lending Agreement. Whether any Shareholder-specific matching obligation exists is unclear.

The liquidity risk paragraph never discloses that c033 permits up to 15% of total assets in illiquid securities, describing the exposure only as arising "when it invests in particular investments, which are difficult to purchase or sell." The disclosure and the policy limit sit awkwardly together.

The offering is said to be made "privately to a limited number of investors" without stating the number, while Declaration of Trust Section 4.4 and recital (c) cap participation at fewer than 100 Shareholders and Rule 506 has its own investor limits. What limit actually binds the offering is unresolved between the documents.

Reliance on Section 3(c)(7), which requires that all beneficial owners be "qualified purchasers," cannot be squared with c001's offering to "qualified institutional purchasers" or the cover legend's "qualified institutional or accredited investors." The class of investors who may hold Shares differs depending on which passage is followed.

"Appropriate representations and undertakings" to assure "these conditions of 'beneficial ownership'" specifies neither the representations required nor the mechanism for ongoing assurance. Both "appropriate" and the referenced "conditions" are left without content in this sentence.

"It is not anticipated at this time that there will be any ERISA Plan investors in the CI Term Trust" cannot be squared with Declaration of Trust Sections 3.3 and 8.5, which impose an ERISA prudence standard and preserve ERISA liability for plan Shareholders, or with the Subscription Agreement's ERISA fiduciary representation. Whether plan investors are contemplated is left contradictory across the documents.

Allocation of income, gain, loss and deduction "as determined according to the Declaration of Trust" must be read against Section 9.1 of the Declaration as replaced by the First Amendment, which prescribes capital accounts and the full netting methodology of Treas. Reg. 1.704-3(e)(3)(v) while the unamended Section 9.1 declared the Trust "not a partnership." The governing allocation rule requires reading the instruments together.

"Wells Fargo may request an opinion from KPMG LLP from time to time" creates no entitlement in Shareholders to any tax opinion and no standard for when one will be sought. Whether investors may rely on the possibility of such an opinion is left open.

"Should be exempt from taxation by the State of Maryland" and "should not cause a Shareholder to be subject to tax in Maryland" are hedged predictions, and "absent any other nexus to Maryland" is undefined. Whether any representation is made at all, and on what condition, is unclear from the words used.

Describing the Memorandum's purpose as "to provide an overview of the CI Term Trust and its policies" sits against Section V's mandatory language that investments "shall comply with the following portfolio guidelines," and against the cover legend qualifying the Memorandum in its entirety by reference to the Declaration of Trust. Whether the investment guidelines are binding obligations or mere description turns on this provision.

The invitation to review "any other materials available to Wells Fargo relating to the Trust, the CI Term Trust and the terms of offering" has no ascertainable boundary and no stated procedure or obligation to produce. What documents a prospective investor is entitled to see is left undefined.

The prohibition on reproduction, distribution or "divulgence of any of its contents" states no duration, no carve-out for legal compulsion or professional advisers, and no identified obligor. Its scope as a confidentiality undertaking is indeterminate on its own words.

The obligation to return the Memorandum on non-subscription or on delivery of updated materials cannot easily be squared with c062's invitation to review it and the Subscription Agreement's provision that the Subscriber relies on the facts and terms set forth in the Confidential Memorandum. Whether a subscriber retains and may rely on the document is left in doubt.
